stories.headline: A six-player jolt—and a season that still slipped away
stories.label: 2025 · Blockbuster trade
stories.context: Charley’s Angels entered Week 5 at 1–3, while All the way to the Em-zone stood 3–1. The deal landed at a clear pivot point for both teams.
stories.decision: Charley K. acquired Patrick Mahomes, Ashton Jeanty and Terry McLaurin. Emma T. received T.J. Hockenson, Brian Thomas Jr. and Baker Mayfield in the same six-player deal.
stories.aftermath: Mahomes and Jeanty supplied 308.26 starting-lineup points for Charley; McLaurin never entered a CGL starting lineup during that stint. Charley won the next 3 games, but finished 6–8 and missed the playoffs. Emma’s return supplied 118.4 starter points, and her team finished 5–9.

stories.headline: A twelfth-round pick became part of a championship deal
stories.label: 2024 · Foundational trade
stories.context: Charley’s Angels and CB’s Bulls were both 1–1 when they completed one of the archive’s largest deals before Week 3.
stories.decision: Charley K. had drafted Chuba Hubbard in Round 12, 142nd overall. Before Week 3, he packaged that late-round pick with Tyreek Hill for D’Andre Swift and A.J. Brown. CB’s Bulls put both Hill and Hubbard to work; all four players became starters for their new teams.
stories.aftermath: Swift and Brown produced 320.6 starter points, including 94.2 in the championship bracket. Hill and Hubbard produced 331.8 for CB’s Bulls. Charley’s Angels finished 13–1 and won the title; CB’s Bulls finished 3–11.
evidence: 94.2 playoff points from Swift and Brown

stories.headline: The first pick went missing. An eleventh-rounder got a second chance.
stories.label: 2024–2025 · Sustained success
stories.context: Timmy K. opened the 2024 draft with Christian McCaffrey at No. 1. McCaffrey’s Achilles trouble kept him out through Week 9, leaving the Timberwolves without their first overall pick for most of the regular season. One answer was a player Timmy had already drafted—and let go.
stories.decision: Chase Brown arrived in Round 11, pick 121. Timmy dropped him for Cam Akers in Week 3, then reversed the move 3 days later. Back with the Timberwolves, Brown became a regular starter and supplied 185.0 points, including 40.2 in the playoffs.
stories.aftermath: The Timberwolves finished 9–5 in 2024. Timmy found more help after draft day the following year: Quinshon Judkins and George Kittle supplied 228.2 starting-lineup points between them, and the team finished 9–5. Across the two seasons, those three additions supplied 413.2 points in 28 starts.

stories.headline: Four defenses, four playoff weeks, one championship
stories.label: 2025 · Championship reinforcements
stories.context: Flux Capacitors entered the 2025 championship bracket as the #4 seed after a 9–5 regular season.
stories.decision: Tony R. used four separate acquisitions for four consecutive playoff weeks: Jacksonville, New Orleans, Pittsburgh and Las Vegas.
stories.aftermath: Each defense made one championship-bracket start and the group scored 61.0 points. Flux Capacitors finished the run as CGL champion.

stories.headline: Tee Higgins crossed the waiver wire—and resurfaced in the playoffs
stories.label: 2024 · The one that got away
stories.context: CB’s Bulls released Tee Higgins while adding Alexander Mattison in Week 2.
stories.decision: The Timberwolves added Higgins the following week and later used him for seven starts.
stories.aftermath: Higgins delivered 124.5 starter points for Timmy K., including 39.6 across two championship-bracket starts. Mattison produced 13.5 points in two starts for CB’s Bulls. A September release had become a December contributor for another contender.

stories.headline: Bucky Irving broke out, even if Mike’s season did not
stories.label: 2024 · Waiver find
stories.context: Mike’s Magic was 0–2 when Bucky Irving arrived before Week 3.
stories.decision: Mike K. added Irving as a free agent and eventually started him eleven times.
stories.aftermath: Irving supplied 161.7 regular-season points, the strongest pickup contribution in the 2024 archive. Mike’s Magic recovered from its winless start to finish 5–9. Irving became a bright spot even as the team missed the playoffs.
